paper.title: Algorithm 684: C1 and C2 interpolation on triangles with quintic and nonic bivariate polynomials

stack: Fortran (TOMS 684 archive: single file 684.gz, algorithm subroutines plus PROGRAM DFC1C2 driver)

claim.text: PROGRAM DFC1C2 (default REAL build) prints COMPUTED VALUE for Z(44,3) on the example's rectangular grid that agrees with the author's expected constant 3.035646151154, tolerance 1e-3 absolute, fixed in the queue entry.

reference.archive: netlib.org/toms/684.gz sha256 d7370718ce36c41ae718fe3061cad733f664427cf78736abb5a0e20e3171dbe3 (684.f is its gunzipped member; PROGRAM DFC1C2 holds the expected constant)

attempt: The archive is a single Fortran file, 684.f (gunzipped from 684.gz, sha256 checked). It ships no Makefile or build line. The file was compiled as shipped with gfortran (conda-forge gcc 16.2.0) and default flags: gfortran -o dfc1c2 684.f, then ./dfc1c2, with no edit. It builds and runs (build_exit=0, run_exit=0); the build only prints Fortran 2018 warnings about old-style DO labels. The first COMPUTED VALUE line is 3.035507202148 against the expected 3.035646151154, a difference of 1.39e-4, inside tol_abs 1e-3. Pass 2 at -O2 in a clean directory gives the same printed value. The driver's second WRITE prints the C2-minus-C1 difference after Z is overwritten; it is not the claimed quantity and is not claimed.

original_attempt.reason: builds and runs with default gfortran flags and no source change; the archive gives no build line, so the plain compile is the only route
